questions.q: What is Azure's ND-series actually built for?
options: Virtual desktop infrastructure and CAD visualization
Serverless function hosting with no GPU at all
Running only Windows Server workloads
Large-scale deep learning training, pairing A100 or H100 GPUs with NVLink within a VM and InfiniBand networking between VMs for distributed, multi-node training
questions.explain: ND A100 v4 and ND H100 v5-series VMs add the GPU-to-GPU (NVLink) and VM-to-VM (InfiniBand) interconnect that multi-node training depends on, distinguishing them from Azure's other GPU families.

questions.q: What is Azure's NV-series designed for, as opposed to ND-series?
options: Visualization and virtual desktop workloads, such as GPU-accelerated remote desktops, CAD, and light inference — not large-scale deep learning training
The exact same training workloads as ND-series, just at a lower price
Running database servers with no GPU involvement
Multi-node distributed training of frontier-scale language models
questions.explain: NV-series VMs (e.g. NVadsA10 v5) target visualization and virtual desktop use cases, not the massive matmul throughput and multi-node interconnect that ND-series targets for training.

questions.q: On AWS, which GPU instance family is the cost-effective line for inference serving and graphics workloads rather than frontier-scale training?
options: P5 instances
P4de instances
G-series instances (e.g. G4dn with T4 GPUs, G5 with A10G GPUs, G6 with L4 GPUs)
P3 instances
questions.explain: AWS's G-series (G4dn, G5, G6) is priced and positioned for inference, graphics, and smaller-scale fine-tuning, while the P-series (P3, P4d/P4de, P5) is the training-focused line with NVLink and EFA networking.

questions.q: Why do AWS P4d/P4de and P5 instances, and Azure's ND-series, add high-bandwidth interconnects like NVLink and EFA/InfiniBand?
options: These interconnects are purely a marketing feature with no effect on training
They only matter for storage throughput, not GPU-to-GPU communication
They are required to run any inference workload, no matter how small
Distributed, multi-node training needs fast GPU-to-GPU communication within a server and fast networking between servers to synchronize gradients efficiently across many GPUs
questions.explain: Multi-node training requires frequent synchronization of gradients across GPUs; NVLink speeds up GPU-to-GPU communication within a server, while EFA/InfiniBand speeds up communication between servers — both are what the training-focused families are built around.

questions.q: Why can an A100 GPU with 80 GB of HBM and a T4 GPU with 16 GB not be treated as interchangeable, even if both appear as 'a GPU' on a cloud instance?
options: A T4 is simply an older, slower version of an A100 with no other practical difference

VRAM capacity determines whether a job's full working set — weights, gradients, optimizer state, and activations — can fit on the card at all, and a job needing 60+ GB will not run on a 16 GB GPU regardless of instance family naming
They are, in fact, fully interchangeable for any training workload
The difference only matters for video rendering, never for machine learning
questions.explain: As covered in Lesson 2, a training job's memory footprint must fit entirely in VRAM; the specific GPU model's memory capacity, not just the presence of 'a GPU,' decides whether a given job can run on that instance at all.
